 Vs.
 The Union of India & Ors.
 Mr. Kishore Dutta,
 Mr. P. C. Das,
 Mr. Atul Prasanth..............for the petitioners.
 Leave to move the writ petition without service of notice on the  respondents is granted having regard to the urgency involved in the writ petition.
An order dated 21.09.2016 issued by the Commissioner of Food Safety, Andaman and Nicobar Islands (hereafter the commissioner) is under challenge in this writ petition.

Invoking the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (hereafter the 2006 Act) read with the regulations framed thereunder, the commissioner prohibited "the manufacture, storage,
distribution and sale of all forms of processed/flavoured/scented chewing tobacco, whether going by the name or form of Gutka, Pan Masala, Zarda packed and unpacked/loose, tobacco leaf in any form etc; and pan masala based sugar boiled based confectioneries in the entire Union Territory of Andaman and Nicobar Islands for a period of one year from 2nd October, 2016 in the interest of public health."

Mr. Dutta, learned senior advocate representing the petitioners has contended as follows:
1. The 2006 Act does not apply to tobacco and tobacco products and, therefore,
invocation of provisions thereof is illegal and absolutely unauthorized.

According to him, the Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Shri P. Selvaraj & Ors vs The Union Of India & Ors on 4 October, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56200172/

sentences.text: The commissioner who issued the impugned order is the Director of Health Services, Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
She has been entrusted with additional charge of the office of Commissioner of Food Safety for the Union Territory of Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

sentences.text: In terms of regulation 2.1.1 of the Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011, no person below the rank of "Commissioner and Secretary" to the State Government shall be eligible to be appointed as the Commissioner of Food Safety.

The incumbent holding additional charge of the office of Commissioner of Food Safety, not being an officer at the secretary level, could not have been entrusted with the charge of the office of the Commissioner of Food Safety.
The contentions urged by Mr. Dutta in support of the prayer for interim relief have been duly considered.
This Bench is afraid, interim relief at this stage is uncalled for because of the reasons that follow.

Food is defined in section 3(j) of the 2006 Act as follows:
(j) "food" means any substance, whether processed, partially processed or unprocessed, which is intended for human consumption and includes......................."
Regulation 2.3.4 of the Food Safety And Standards (Prohibition and Restrictions on Sales)
Regulations, 2011 provides that "tobacco and nicotine shall not be used as ingredients in any food products".

sentences.text:
Having regard to the definition of "food" as extracted (supra), there can be no doubt that gutka, pan masala, zarda etc. are consumed by none other than human beings and are, therefore,
covered by the meaning of the word "food".
It also appears from the Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011 that 'pan masala' is a food product for which a standard has been prescribed.

Since these food products contain tobacco and nicotine,
prima facie, the prohibitory order issued by the commissioner does not commend to this Bench to have been issued illegally and without authority of law.

sentences.text: Assuming that the 2006 Act has no application to tobacco and tobacco products and it is covered by the 2003 Act, it is noticed from section 6 thereof that the same contemplates prohibition of sale of cigarettes or other tobacco products.

According to Mr. Dutta, to make a prohibitory order,
conditions mentioned against clauses (a) and (b) both have to be fulfilled.

For facility of reference, section 6 of the 2003 Act is quoted below:
"6. Prohibition on sale of cigarettes or other tobacco products to a person below the age of eighteen years and in particular area.

- No person shall sell, offer for sale, or permit sale of, cigarette or any other tobacco product - (a) to any person who is under eighteen years of age, and (b) in an area within a radius of one hundred yards of any educational institution."
In the considered prima facie view of this Bench, "and" between clauses (a) and (b) ought to be read as "or"; or else, sale of cigarettes or other tobacco products to persons under eighteen years of age could be transacted at an area just beyond a radius of one hundred yards of any educational institution.
That could not have been intention of the legislature.

It, therefore, stands to reason that prohibition could be ordered for sale of cigarettes or other tobacco products to any person who is a minor; prohibition could also be ordered for sale of cigarettes or other tobacco products in an area within a radius of one hundred yards of any educational institution.

To overcome section 6, it was necessary for the petitioners to plead that they have been carrying on business in sale of tobacco products not within a radius of one hundred yards of any educational institution.

Such pleading is, however, absent and, therefore, even if the 2006 Act may not be applicable, the impugned order could be sustained on the ground that incorrect reference to a statute would not render the order vitiated, if the source of power could be traced to some other statute.
The Division Bench decision of the Patna High Court in M/s.
Omkar Agency (supra) has been perused.

Although the Division Bench has given elaborate reasons for the findings arrived by it, the same does not have the effect of tying down the hands of the union territory administration to issue an order of the nature impugned herein.

For the reasons given by this Bench while holding that invocation of the 2006 Act by the commissioner is prima facie not unauthorized, this Bench is not inclined to follow the Division Bench decision at this stage.
The decision reported in Kusum Ingots & Alloys Ltd. (supra) has no application in the facts and circumstances of the present case as no statutory provision has been set aside.
If only a statutory provision had been set aside, it would cease to be applicable for the rest of the country.
That is the law laid down therein.

An executive order passed in respect of a particular State upon being set aside by an order of court having territorial jurisdiction ipso facto cannot be made applicable in respect of the rest of the country.

Insofar as the decision in Pradip J. Mehta (supra) is concerned, it would appear from paragraph 23 thereof that the Supreme Court stressed the need for the High Courts to either record its agreement or dissent with the decision of any other High Court that is placed before it.

It was also stressed that the High Court, which differs with the view taken by the other High Court, in all fairness, must Shri P. Selvaraj & Ors vs The Union Of India & Ors on 4 October, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56200172/
3 record its dissent with reasons therefor.

sentences.text: That has exactly been followed by this Bench while holding the 2006 Act to be applicable in respect of food like pan masala, gutka, zarda etc.
The contention raised by Mr. Dutta based on the decision in M/s. Omkar Agency (supra) does not impress this Bench for granting interim relief to the petitioners.

Insofar as the point that the incumbent holding additional charge as Commissioner of Food Safety does not possess requisite qualification is concerned, there is no specific averment in the writ petition that the incumbent is not holding the rank of a Secretary to the union territory administration.
Vague allegations have been levelled that the incumbent is not qualified to hold additional charge of Commissioner of Food Safety.
In view of such vague allegations, no credence can be given to the same at least at this stage.
There is one other fundamental aspect that needs to be taken care of.
Here, individual rights of businessmen are pitted against the basic right conferred on each and every citizen of the country including the residents of the islands by Article 21 of the Constitution.

In the event the impugned order is stayed and the petitioners are allowed to involve themselves in the business of sale of pan masala, gutka, zarda etc. and upon consumption thereof the health of any citizen is adversely affected but ultimately the writ petition fails, it would be impossible to retrieve the situation for such affected citizen.

On the contrary, if the impugned order is allowed to be operative for the time being and ultimately the writ petition succeeds with the result that the impugned order is set aside, it is only the business interest of a few like the petitioners that would be affected.
Right to life of citizens must obviously prevail over individual rights to carry on business guaranteed by Article 19 of the Constitution.

The impugned order records that the same has been issued in the interest of public health and, therefore, this Bench in exercise of its discretionary writ powers refuses to stay the operation of the order impugned.
It is, however, observed that the impugned order shall abide by the result of the writ petition.
Let affidavit-in-opposition be filed by the respondents by 18.11.2016; reply thereto, if any, may be filed within 25.11.2016.
The petitioners shall be at liberty to mention the writ petition for consideration after exchange of affidavits before the available Circuit Bench, subject to convenience of the learned judge.
In the meanwhile, copy of the writ petition should be served on all the respondents within a week from date and an affidavit of service filed on the returnable date.

The records of the writ petition shall be transmitted to the Circuit Bench at Port Blair, Andaman &
Nicobar Islands immediately.
Photostat copy of this order, duly counter-signed by the Assistant Registrar (Court), be handed over to the learned advocate for the petitioners on the usual undertaking.

(DIPANKAR DATTA, J.)
